diagram_math_checks.check: Boundary arcs have radii 0.75 and 1.25 and radial sides have angles ±45 degrees. All four are dashed and captioned excluded, matching the strict Example domain inequalities.

Orange radius-one arc spans exactly -30 to +30 degrees. Its lower/upper filled endpoints equal X(-a,0)=(√3/2,-1/2) and X(a,0)=(√3/2,1/2). They are included in the path and are the global minima by proof step 1.2; the figure asserts no uniqueness of MEPs.

At the arc midpoint the tangent arrow points vertically upward, consistent with increasing s and R parameter; normal points horizontally outward, consistent with X_n=N and increasing n in step 1.1. Arrows represent directions, not unit-length drawn segments. Step 2.1 supplies exactly one negative Hessian eigenvalue at this point.

Crossed Cartesian origin lies outside the dashed annular sector since its radius is zero. It is distinct from chart coordinate pair (s,n)=(0,0), whose image is (1,0); no collision point is introduced into U.

Definition of regular MEP imposes the vanishing normal gradient component and fixed endpoints; original step 1.1 verifies this analytically, independently of the picture. Original Example/Facts/Proof and suppliers were not edited.
